question: Does exact one-action-chunk best-of-K selection provide enough closed-loop benefit to justify a learned Q selector?

policy.architecture: native BitVLA with ternary BitWAM world head

evaluation.other_candidates: temporally smoothed Gaussian perturbations in six continuous action dimensions
evaluation.candidate_nesting: fixed per-episode RNG makes lower-K candidates a prefix of higher-K candidates
evaluation.selector: maximum exact LIBERO goal predicates satisfied after one eight-action chunk
evaluation.tie_break: retain the earliest candidate, so equal scores retain the base action
evaluation.branch_isolation: camera-free MuJoCo ControlEnv in a separate spawned process
evaluation.control_observations: normal camera observations in the main environment

hardware.pairing_control: Each task used the same physical GPU for K=1, K=4, and K=16.

quality_controls: Counterfactual simulation is process-isolated from the control environment and random state.
Earlier in-process and rendered-worker diagnostic runs were archived and excluded.
All ten task shards completed for every reported condition.
